done_when: On a runner without gh, the nightly full-test result step sets up Python, posts the forge-full-suite status with Python's standard library, reads the token from the environment, and passes or fails to match the full run.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Gate. The supplied proof list is marked `missing`, so the Done-when details are not mapped to named tests and their pull-request results. The new test at this location exists, but the required proof list is still absent.
Case: normal use - Forge reviews the nightly result fix before merge.
findings.title: Gate: proof list

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test. The test bypasses the result job's Python setup and token wiring, so it can pass when the nightly run cannot post a status. It executes only the extracted script with its own Python and `GH_TOKEN`; the assertion at line 161 checks only that setup appears somewhere in the job. Moving setup after the reporter or removing the token binding at `.github/workflows/forge.yml:261` and `src/forge/prcheck.py:337` would leave this test passing while the real job fails. The existing group test checks the result binding at `tests/test_nightly_group_results.py:77`, but not these prerequisites. The new test also rejects an otherwise valid implementation that uses checkout.
Case: normal use - A nightly result runs on a fresh runner without gh or preinstalled Python.
findings.title: Gate: test_3_full_test_result_is_posted_without_gh

why: Bug 1524. On a self-hosted or new-each-job runner without the GitHub command-line tool (gh), the nightly full-test result step fails, so the full-suite status is never posted.
